messages:
maya: heads up — noticed p95 for /v1/generate jumped ~250ms at 09:14 UTC after yesterday's quota routing tweak. dashboard shows counts stable but p95 moved only for that canonical endpoint. :thinking:
omar: ugh. is this the fallback routing change where we let low-tier traffic hit the burst pool?
chris: asked earlier — could be aggregation losing the route tag when requests hit the quota-fallback proxy. if the dashboard rollup strips route tags we end up mixing fast and slow paths under same endpoint.
maya: exactly. console shows two series in the raw stream: route=primary (low-latency) and route=quota-fallback (higher latency because of queueing). but the percentiles on the endpoint page are computed after rollup that drops route label. so p95 seems terrible even though client-facing route stayed fine.
li: can we confirm counts by origin? quick query: 
```
SELECT route_tag, quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, count() as n FROM latency_raw WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY route_tag
```
chris: run that against raw samples — that'll show if fallback is the spike source. also check sample_source header: quota-proxy currently marks origin=quota-fallback, but our rollup job renormalizes to endpoint only.
maya: i ran it — quota-fallback has p95 ~420ms, primary ~80ms, but endpoint rollup p95 is ~350ms. counts: fallback is only 8% of traffic. seems like our rollup merging algorithm uses weighted tdigest without tagging, so small high-latency tail skews p95.
omar: why would an 8% subset change p95 so much? are we accidentally double-counting or replaying?
chris: tdigest merge is sensitive to high-value outliers if the merge weights are off. i suspect the merge is using per-shard counts but not normalizing for downsampled samples. basically the fallback path samples at a higher rate to preserve tail, then rollup assumes uniform sampling.
maya: ah — quota-proxy sets sample_rate=1 for fallback, rate=0.1 for primary. rollup multiplies by shard_count instead of effective_sampled_count. that inflates the influence of fallback.
li: proposed quick mitigation: annotate rollup with sample_origin and expose a p95_by_route on endpoint detail; second, change rollup to use effective_sampled_count = sum(1/sample_rate) instead of naive counts.
omar: short-term dashboard tweak would help product teams. long-term fix in rollup logic is needed.
chris: agree. patch idea: in merge step use weight = observed_count * sample_rate_correction where sample_rate_correction = 1/expected_sample_rate. also add a flag to console to show sample_rate distribution.
maya: i'll open a tiny RFC and PR. PR will: 1) change rollup weight calculation 2) add pctl_by_route metric on endpoint page 3) add a console note when sample_rate variance > 5x.
devex-bot: deploy-checklist created: RFC-6472, PR-8391, dashboard-issue-1287. blockers?
chris: only question — do we have reliable sample_rate metadata everywhere? some older proxies don't emit it. fallback path does, main path not always.
li: we can backfill by assuming default_sample_rate when missing, but mark those series as partial. dashboard should display a small warning.
omar: cool. can we also add an endpoint health check that alerts when small-signal p95 moves >30% vs cohort? want early warning before product notices.
maya: yes, will include an alert playbook in RFC. timeframe: quick dashboard flag this week, rollup fix early next week.
chris: FYI I'll add unit tests for tdigest merges with nonuniform sampling. learned that the merge math is subtle.
maya: thanks all. filing notes on customer impact and linking to the revert plan in case fix regresses. :thumbsup:
